title: Small-Shop Layout
description: A small-shop layout puts the workbench at the center, raw material storage near the door, and machines along the walls so that long boards can move through the shop without crossing a walkway. This guide lays out a 12 by 16 foot shop in four zones: bench, cutting, assembly, and storage, with a 42 inch main aisle kept clear at all times. Lumber enters at the door, goes to the cutting zone, then to the bench, then to assembly, so work flows in one direction and offcuts never pile up where people walk.

image.description: Dimensioned sketch of Small-Shop Layout: overall 144 x 192 x 96 in in, showing the plan/elevation outline with dimension labels and key features of the design.
image.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="400" height="240" viewBox="0 0 400 240"><rect x="50" y="60" width="288" height="150" fill="none" stroke="#333" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="50" y="230" width="70" height="28" fill="none" stroke="#333"/><text x="53" y="247" font-size="9">Bench</text><rect x="128" y="230" width="70" height="28" fill="none" stroke="#333"/><text x="131" y="247" font-size="9">Cutting</text><rect x="206" y="230" width="70" height="28" fill="none" stroke="#333"/><text x="209" y="247" font-size="9">Assembly</text><rect x="284" y="230" width="70" height="28" fill="none" stroke="#333"/><text x="287" y="247" font-size="9">Storage</text><line x1="50" y1="222" x2="338" y2="222" stroke="#333"/><text x="50" y="238" font-size="11">144.0 in wide</text><text x="50" y="52" font-size="11">Small-Shop Layout</text></svg>

specs.tolerances: Zone boundaries within 2 in; aisle clearance never below 36 in.
specs.arithmetic_note: Layout totals: 4 zones covering 87.0 sq ft; every aisle clearance is at least 36 in (minimum aisle 42 in), so walkways stay clear of the work zones.

steps: Measure the room and mark the four zones on the floor with tape.
Place the bench where daylight falls across the work surface.
Put lumber storage by the door and machines along the walls.
Mark the 42 inch main aisle and keep it clear.
Walk a full board through the flow once before fixing anything down.

tools.safety_notes: Wear eye and hearing protection whenever power tools run; keep blades guarded and hands clear of cutting paths; keep dust under control and walkways clear.

demo.code:
# Workshop layout checker: zone areas, aisle clearances, circuit loads
ZONES = [('Bench', 72, 30), ('Cutting', 96, 48), ('Assembly', 72, 48), ('Storage', 96, 24)]
AISLES = [42, 48]
CIRCUITS = [('General', 20, 8), ('Lighting', 15, 6)]
total = 0.0
for name, w, d in ZONES:
    area = w * d / 144.0
    total += area
    print("%s: %d x %d in = %.1f sq ft" % (name, w, d, area))
print("Total zone area: %.1f sq ft" % total)
for i, a in enumerate(AISLES, 1):
    print("Aisle %d: %d in clear - %s" % (i, a, "PASS (>=36 in)" if a >= 36 else "FAIL"))
for name, amps, load in CIRCUITS:
    print("%s: %d A load on %d A circuit = %.0f%%" % (name, load, amps, load / amps * 100.0))
demo.expected_output:
Bench: 72 x 30 in = 15.0 sq ft
Cutting: 96 x 48 in = 32.0 sq ft
Assembly: 72 x 48 in = 24.0 sq ft
Storage: 96 x 24 in = 16.0 sq ft
Total zone area: 87.0 sq ft
Aisle 1: 42 in clear - PASS (>=36 in)
Aisle 2: 48 in clear - PASS (>=36 in)
General: 8 A load on 20 A circuit = 40%
Lighting: 6 A load on 15 A circuit = 40%

Heavy tools sit low, sharp edges face the wall or a guard, and the panel leaves the bench clear for work.

title: Shop Lighting

This guide places four 48 inch LED shop lights over a 12 by 16 foot shop, two over the bench and two over the cutting zone, hung 7 feet above the floor and wired on a single switched circuit. Lights are chosen for a high color-rendering rating so wood colors read true, and no light sits where it will shine straight into the operator's eyes.

title: Workbench Build
description: A workbench is the shop's main work surface, and this guide builds a sturdy 72 by 30 inch bench, 36 inches high, from a 3/4 inch plywood top over a laminated pine frame with a lower shelf. The top is flat and heavy enough to hold work steady, the legs are braced on all four sides, and the bench is leveled with adjustable feet so it does not rock. A bench built this way holds a vise, supports full-size panels, and stays put under hand-planing force.

title: Dust Collection Basics
description: Dust collection captures sawdust at the machine before it fills the shop air, protecting lungs and keeping the shop clean. This guide connects a 1 horsepower collector to a table saw and a miter saw with 4 inch hose, blast gates at each machine, and a separator bin that drops out heavy chips before the filter. Hoses run short and straight, gates stay closed on machines not in use, and the filter is cleaned on a fixed schedule.

Fit blast gates at each machine.

title: Shop Electrical Safety Basics
description: Shop electrical safety keeps power tools, lighting, and dust collection on circuits that can carry their loads without overheating. This guide maps a small shop's circuits, labels the panel, fits ground-fault protection where water or concrete floors are present, and sets rules: one major machine per circuit, cords inspected before use, and no daisy-chained power strips. title: Noise Control

title: Shop Heating and Ventilation

This guide sizes a vented heater for a 12 by 16 foot shop, places it away from dust and finishing areas, adds a make-up air vent, and sets a rule that finishes cure only with ventilation running.
